liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **High Time** (1 review, 1 other source): Reviewer suggests this may be the most epic High Time ever played; Tuning and a New Speedway Boogie tease follow High Time, before Dire Wolf [1][3]
- **Not Fade Away** (2 reviews): Reviewer says the Not Fade Away ends with the band going wild; Reviewer says the section from Not Fade Away into Drums shreds, with outrageous band energy [4][10]
- **Black Peter** (1 review): Reviewer says Jerry's voice sounds pretty and may have found a favorite Black Peter [11]
- **Good Lovin'** (1 review): Reviewer says the Good Lovin' smokes [4]
- **The Other One** (1 review): After the first verse of The Other One, the band hits a moment that draws a notable audience reaction [12]
- **Turn On Your Lovelight** (1 review): Reviewer describes the Lovelight as big [7]

## The recordings

- **gd70-03-07.aud.hanno.6156.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): audience recording; 11 songs; 73 min; rated 3.29/5 by 24 [1]. Said about its sound: Reviewer calls the sound quality very poor, with audience reactions coming through more clearly than the band's playing; Reviewer considers it an excellent-sounding room tape for its period; Reviewer rates the recording as average quality but more than listenable, especially for the period [2][3][7][8]

## Around the show

- During Lovelight, the tape captures audience members chatting inanely and screaming loudly between comments [10]
- The crowd screams at the start of Good Lovin', which the reviewer finds exciting [11]
- Compared with the 2-13-70 show, this one has less subtlety but makes up for it with intense energy [12]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd70-03-07.aud.hanno.6156.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Hanno Bunjes and Uli Teute; source: Audience [1]
